requirements.title: Authority and precedence

acceptanceCriteria.text: This document is the authority for where Causa keeps investigation state, how it saves to GitHub, and how it reports save state.

For Causa it takes precedence over, and supersedes, any persistence, offline, local-durability, synchronization-queue or cross-tab statement in the documents ranked (4) to (7) by ADRP-001, and over the long-term platform documents listed in [docs/rehearsal-007/DEFECT-TRACEABILITY.md](rehearsal-007/DEFECT-TRACEABILITY.md).
Where such a statement conflicts with this document, this document holds and the conflict is not a STOP under ADRP-001.
The frozen causa-data v1.0.0 storage contract and owner decision OD-INDY-9 still govern paths, file sets, serialization, atomicity and read-back; this document refines them and changes none of them.
Acceptance: PAT-14 verifies that the requirements validator finds no conflicting statement in the baseline documents.

requirements.title: Each browser tab holds its own investigation state

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each browser tab MUST hold its own, independent investigation state in F# WebAssembly memory: the investigations it has loaded, the branch head each was loaded or saved at, its unsaved changes, and its save state.
A tab MUST NOT read or write another tab's state.
Opening the same investigation in two tabs gives two independent copies; a change in one tab MUST NOT appear in the other until it has been saved to GitHub and the other tab loads it from GitHub.
Navigation between routes inside one tab MUST keep that tab's state in memory, so moving between investigations or views never loses unsaved changes.
Acceptance: PAT-01 verifies tab independence in a real browser.

requirements.title: No shared browser storage for investigations

acceptanceCriteria.text: Investigation documents, events, snapshots, manifests, unsaved changes, pending commands, save state, branch heads and write markers MUST NOT be written to localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, the Origin Private File System, cookies, a service worker, a shared worker or a BroadcastChannel.
Only non-investigation preferences, such as tour dismissal (UI-012) or theme, may use browser storage, and they MUST NOT contain investigation content, repository paths or credentials.
Credentials stay memory-only (EXT-DATA-004, OD-INDY-10).
The browser's ordinary HTTP cache of the application's static assets is not investigation storage.

Acceptance: PAT-01 inspects every browser store after edits and saves and verifies that none holds investigation content, and PAT-13 verifies that the production artifact contains no call that writes investigation content to a browser store.

requirements.title: No cross-tab locking or coordination

acceptanceCriteria.text: Correctness MUST NOT depend on cross-tab locking or messaging.
The application MUST NOT use `navigator.locks` (Web Locks), a storage lease or a cross-tab message channel to coordinate investigation writes.
Two tabs that save are two independent GitHub writers, and their concurrency is resolved only by the GitHub rules in PERSIST-007 to PERSIST-013.
Acceptance: PAT-11 verifies that every persistence test passes with `navigator.locks` removed from the page, and PAT-13 verifies that the production artifact references no Web Locks API.

requirements.title: GitHub is the authoritative durable store

acceptanceCriteria.text: The connected GitHub repository branch MUST be the only durable store of Causa investigations.
An investigation is opened by reading it from GitHub at a branch head and verifying it as a reader would (causa-data v1.0.0 §11).
The tab records the commit it read as the investigation's base head.
Branch-head reads MUST bypass HTTP caches, and file reads MUST name the commit they read.
Acceptance: PAT-10 verifies that an investigation opened in a new tab equals its last confirmed commit on GitHub.

requirements.title: One atomic commit per save, with an expected head

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every save MUST publish exactly one GitHub commit through one GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` mutation, as OD-INDY-9 defines.
The commit MUST contain the investigation's events append, manifest and snapshot together.
Its `expectedHeadOid` MUST be the branch head the change was decided at, or the head it was rebased onto under PERSIST-009.
A save MUST NOT use per-file Contents API writes, a forced ref update, or any write without an expected head.
Before sending, the adapter MUST check that the commit changes files only under the investigation's own path prefix (causa-data v1.0.0 §9.4.4).
A tab MUST have at most one commit mutation in flight at a time; further save requests in that tab wait in memory until it settles.
Acceptance: PAT-02 records every mutation the application sends and verifies each one against this requirement.

requirements.title: A save is confirmed only after GitHub confirms it

acceptanceCriteria.text: A save is confirmed only when GitHub has returned the new commit for that mutation and a re-read at that commit returns the bytes the save wrote (causa-data v1.0.0 §9.4.3).
Only a confirmed save may move the investigation to Saved and advance its base head.
Changes made in the tab while the save was in flight MUST remain unsaved after it is confirmed.
Acceptance: PAT-02 and PAT-10 verify that Saved appears only after the read-back, and PAT-12 verifies that no other transition reaches Saved.

requirements.title: Detect a stale head

acceptanceCriteria.text: When GitHub refuses a mutation because the branch head is no longer the expected head, the application MUST classify the answer as a stale head: nothing was written, and the change stays unsaved in memory.
It MUST classify each provider answer from its typed content, and MUST keep a stale head distinct from a network failure, an authentication or permission failure, a rate limit and a validation error.
A network failure MUST NOT be reported as a stale head or a conflict.
Acceptance: PAT-03 verifies each classification with the stateful GitHub fake and against the live test repository.

requirements.title: Rebase automatically over unrelated changes

acceptanceCriteria.text: After a stale head, the application MUST read the new branch head and compare the investigation's files at the base head and at the new head.
When those files are unchanged, the branch moved only for unrelated changes, such as another investigation saved by this tab, another tab or another device.
The application MUST then re-verify the remote history, keep the same events, manifest and snapshot, and send the commit again with the new head as `expectedHeadOid`, without asking the user.
While it does so, the investigation stays Saving.
Acceptance: PAT-04 verifies that a change saves without user action after unrelated commits advance the branch, and that the unrelated commits stay on the branch.

requirements.title: Limit automatic rebases

acceptanceCriteria.text: One save request MUST make at most three automatic rebase attempts, so it sends at most four commit mutations in total.
Every attempt MUST follow a fresh read of the branch head.
When the limit is reached, the investigation MUST move to Save failed, with the cause that the repository kept changing, and keep the change unsaved in memory until the user asks to save again.
Acceptance: PAT-08 verifies that a branch that advances before every attempt receives no more than four mutations for one save request.

requirements.title: Preserve unsaved changes when the same investigation changed remotely

acceptanceCriteria.text: When the investigation's own files differ between the base head and the new head, another writer has saved the same investigation, and this is a genuine conflict.
This includes another tab of the same user.
The application MUST NOT rebase, merge or overwrite automatically.
It MUST move the investigation to Conflict and keep every unsaved change unchanged in memory, still visible in the tab.
An investigation deleted or rewritten on the branch is also a conflict.
Acceptance: PAT-05 verifies that the unsaved change is kept, nothing is sent, and the other writer's commit stays on the branch.

requirements.title: Resolve a genuine conflict only by explicit user choice

acceptanceCriteria.text: A conflict MUST stay in Conflict until the user chooses a resolution.
The application MUST offer three actions: review the differences, reapply my changes to the GitHub version, and discard my changes and load the GitHub version.
Reapply MUST load the GitHub version and re-decide each unsaved command, in its original order, through the F# domain engine at that version.
Accepted commands become unsaved changes on the new base head; refused commands MUST be listed with the engine's reason and MUST NOT be applied.
Reapply MUST NOT save; the user saves the result.
Discard MUST ask for confirmation first.
The application MUST NOT offer any action that replaces the GitHub version with the tab's version.
Acceptance: PAT-05 verifies each action and that no action overwrites the other writer's commit.

requirements.title: Never silently overwrite another commit

acceptanceCriteria.text: No write may remove, replace or hide a commit made by another writer.
The application MUST NOT force-push, reset a ref, delete and recreate files, or write against a head it has not read from GitHub in the current tab session.
Every other writer's commit MUST remain reachable from the branch head after any sequence of saves, rebases, reconciliations and conflict resolutions.
Acceptance: PAT-02, PAT-04 and PAT-05 verify after each scenario that every commit made by every writer is still reachable from the branch head.

requirements.title: Unique write markers

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each tab MUST create a random session identifier in memory when it starts.
Each commit mutation MUST carry a write marker made of that identifier and a sequence number, as a trailer in the commit message.
Markers are audit metadata used only for reconciliation (causa-data v1.0.0 §9.4.5), and MUST be unique across tabs, devices and page loads.
Acceptance: PAT-02 verifies marker uniqueness across concurrent tabs and reloads.

requirements.title: Reconcile an unknown commit outcome before retrying

acceptanceCriteria.text: When a mutation may have reached GitHub but no recognised answer came back, the outcome is unknown.
This covers a timeout, a lost response, a dropped connection after sending, and any answer the code does not recognise.
The investigation MUST move to Unknown commit outcome and MUST NOT send another mutation for it until reconciliation decides the outcome.
Reconciliation reads the branch head and the commits after the expected head.
If a commit carries this save's marker and its tree holds the written bytes, the save is confirmed.
If a commit carries the marker but the bytes differ, the investigation moves to Save failed and is not reported as saved.
If the branch head still equals the expected head and no commit carries the marker, nothing was written, and the save may be sent again within the PERSIST-010 limit.
If the head moved and no commit carries the marker, the change was not written and the stale-head rules apply.
If the expected head is no longer an ancestor of the branch head, the investigation moves to Save failed with the cause that the branch history was rewritten.
If a reconciliation read fails, the investigation stays Unknown commit outcome.
Acceptance: PAT-06 verifies every branch of this rule with injected lost answers.

requirements.title: Bounded retries and no tight loops

acceptanceCriteria.text: Automatic network activity for one save request MUST be bounded.
Commit mutations are limited by PERSIST-010.

Reconciliation of one unknown outcome MUST make at most three automatic reads, at least 2 seconds, 4 seconds and 8 seconds apart, plus one read each time the browser goes from offline to online; after that it waits for the user to choose Check again.
A save that fails before it is sent MUST NOT be retried automatically.
Under a network that fails every request, one save request MUST cause at most four commit mutations and at most four reconciliation reads in 60 seconds.

requirements.title: Meaning of each save state

acceptanceCriteria.text: The seven states have these entry conditions, words and actions:
Saved: the last save was confirmed under PERSIST-007 and the tab holds no unsaved change.
The lozenge reads "Saved", and the freshness line gives the commit time.
No action is offered.
Unsaved: the tab holds changes that have not been sent, and the application is online.
The text says the changes exist only in this tab.
The action is Save.
Saving: a commit mutation is being prepared or is in flight, or an automatic rebase or reconciliation read is running.
The text says the change is being saved to GitHub and is not yet confirmed.
No save action is offered.
Offline: the application is offline and the tab holds unsaved changes.
The text says the changes exist only in this tab and cannot be saved until the connection returns.
Save is offered only after the connection returns.
Conflict: PERSIST-011 applies.
The text says another writer changed this investigation on GitHub, nothing of this tab's change was written, and the tab's changes are kept.
The actions are the three of PERSIST-012.
Unknown commit outcome: PERSIST-015 applies.
The text says the save may or may not have reached GitHub and that the application is checking.
Save is not offered; Check again is offered after the automatic reads are spent.
Save failed: GitHub refused the save for a reason other than a stale head, the rebase limit was reached, or a reconciliation found a mismatch or rewritten history.
The text names the cause and says the changes are kept in this tab.
The action is Retry when a retry can succeed, or Reconnect when the credential was refused.
When the application is offline and the tab holds no unsaved change, the indicator stays Saved and the workspace header shows that the application is offline.
Acceptance: PAT-15 verifies each state's entry condition, words and actions, and PAT-12 verifies that the machine reaches each state only from its entry condition.

designContracts.rule: Workspace shell, navigation and header come from Forma's workspace-shell, navigation-shell, site-header and skip-link patterns (layout contract reuse[0]).
Save-state indicator: Forma status lozenge naming the state plus freshness in the investigation header.
Loading and errors: the shell renders before WASM with a Forma skeleton; failures use Forma fault patterns.
Navigation: two levels with the Forma navigation shell; under 48rem it collapses through Forma's own pattern, never a custom menu.
web/causa.css may read any --ef-* property in the inventory and must not declare a new one; colours come only from semantic tokens, never from primitives or literals (tokens.rule; FL-10).

conflicts.description: Forma version: the v4.1.2 layout contract's inventory is Forma 0.12.0 (tarball sha256 b824568d…), but the T0 bootstrap (Conditor 0.10.20 + requirements-compiler v41 --bootstrap) installs @echelon-foundry/design-system 0.13.0.
conflicts.disposition: Reported, not resolved. The observer checks pattern classes that exist in both 0.12.0 (inventory) and the installed 0.13.0 (all.css), so the conflict does not change any finding; it needs an owner disposition.

conflicts.description: Package status: requirements-compiled/v4.1.2/README.md and package-manifest.json say CANDIDATE, while AGENTS.md and R9-READINESS-HANDOFF.md state v4.1.2 is approved (APR-V412-OWNER-3) and frozen at tag indy-init-requirements-v4.1.2.
conflicts.disposition: The compiler never writes FROZEN (package-manifest statusMeaning); the tag and the owner's approval record make it frozen. The observer treats v4.1.2 as frozen. No scope is narrowed.

conflicts.description: Rehearsal 9 scope wording: OD-INDY-20 says the ten content gaps are 'in scope for Rehearsal 9' and the catalog drives a catalog-only verification workflow; FINAL-READINESS.md ('Unchanged: every v4.1.2 P0 obligation') and the R9 Verification gate (whole frozen v4.1.2 plan) keep the frozen plan in scope. No source says the frozen plan is out of scope.
conflicts.disposition: Not a true conflict: the catalog adds scope; it does not replace the frozen plan. The observer uses the union and does not select the narrower reading. A builder reading OD-INDY-20 as the whole scope is reported as scope narrowing.
